history.ask: Speed of spread of the redness
options: Spreading over hours, visibly worse same day
Static or slowly changing over weeks

history.ask: Severity of pain relative to what the skin looks like
options: Pain far worse than the skin appearance
Wound, ulcer, or scratch at the site

history.ask: Is the pain centered on a joint?
options: Yes — base of the big toe or another joint, worse at night
No — skin and soft tissue only

history.ask: A soft or pointing area in the swelling

options: Recurrent leg redness in the same leg

red_flags: Pain out of proportion, rapid hour-by-hour spread, dusky or blistering skin, or crepitus — necrotizing fasciitis; urgent surgical referral
Anesthetic patches within the red area — nerve death in necrotizing infection
Hypotension, confusion, or rigors with a skin infection — sepsis
Cellulitis of the face around the eye — orbital involvement threatens vision and the cavernous sinus
Rapidly progressive infection in a diabetic or immunosuppressed patient
exam: Mark the edge of the erythema with a pen and write the time — objective spread on review is a decision-changing finding
Record temperature, BP, pulse, and mental state — quantify systemic toxicity
Palpate the whole area for fluctuance — a drainable collection distinguishes abscess from pure cellulitis
Feel deliberately for crepitus and note any dusky patches, blisters, or bullae
Test skin sensation over the erythema — anesthesia is a necrotizing sign
Examine the border: sharply raised and demarcated (erysipelas) vs diffuse fading edge (cellulitis)
Search for the portal of entry — toe web spaces for tinea, ulcers, bites, injection marks
Look for lymphangitic streaking and palpate the regional nodes
Measure both calves and squeeze gently for deep tenderness when the leg is swollen — DVT does not cause hot spreading erythema but is the classic mimic
Examine the nearby joint through its range — true joint-line pain and restriction point to gout or septic arthritis rather than skin infection
Inspect both legs for hemosiderin staining and venous skin change — bilateral chronic changes suggest stasis dermatitis, not infection

investigations.why: Marked leukocytosis supports abscess or necrotizing infection; a normal count with bilateral chronic changes supports stasis dermatitis
Grades severity — very high values raise necrotizing fasciitis and deep collection above simple cellulitis
Undiagnosed or uncontrolled diabetes drives recurrent abscesses and necrotizing infection; every recurrent skin sepsis deserves this
Renal impairment and sodium derangement accompany necrotizing fasciitis and sepsis, and separate the sick patient from simple cellulitis
Finds the drainable collection cellulitis hides, and defines its depth and size when the exam is equivocal

investigations.test: Pus swab / culture from any drained or discharging point
investigations.why: Identifies the organism in abscess and guides the record for recurrent disease

investigations.test: Venous Doppler ultrasound of the leg
investigations.why: Rules DVT in or out when there is unilateral swelling with risk factors and no clear portal of entry
Supports gout when the picture is joint-centered — though a normal level during the acute attack does not exclude it
